name: Brake disc
summary: A round metal disc that spins with the wheel. The brake pads squeeze it to slow the car.
whatItDoes: It gives the brake pads a hard, flat surface to grip. As the pads clamp it, friction turns the car's movement into heat, and the disc soaks up that heat and sheds it into the air.
howItWorks: The disc sits between the wheel hub and the wheel, so it turns at wheel speed. Many front discs are 'vented': two faces with cooling vanes between them that pump air through as the disc spins. Discs wear thinner over time, and each one has a minimum thickness stamped on it.
failureSymptoms: Vibration through the steering wheel or brake pedal when braking
Deep grooves, or a raised lip around the outer edge
Blue heat marks on the surface
Thickness below the minimum stamped on the disc
safetyNotes: Discs get extremely hot. Let them cool before touching.
Replace discs in pairs on the same axle.
